ask: Write me a short 12-month plan for building a Nigerian fintech portfolio as a document.
reply:
Q: 12-Month Plan: Building a Nigerian Fintech Portfolio Objective Build a focused portfolio of Nigerian fintech companies across pre-seed, seed and Series A, prioritising enterprise software and regulated-market opportunities while maintaining disciplined diligence and portfolio construction. Months 1–3: Define the portfolio and build the pipeline Confirm the annual budget, target number of investments, exposure limits and follow-on reserve. Define the preferred fintech sub-themes, such as payments infrastructure, compliance software, financial data, embedded finance and business banking. Set clear screening criteria: stage, cheque size, founding-team capability, regulatory exposure, customer evidence, revenue quality and capital efficiency. Build a pipeline through founder referrals, operators, accelerators, existing relationships and targeted discovery. Review 30–40 companies and select an initial diligence group. Months 4–6: Run focused diligence and make the first investments Complete structured diligence on the strongest opportunities, covering customers, product, market, competition, regulatory requirements, financials, unit economics and runway. Verify company-reported traction against bank statements, contracts, invoices, cohort data and customer references where appropriate. Make the first one or two investments only where the evidence supports the thesis and the terms are understood. Keep initial positions sized to preserve capital for later investments and follow-ons. Record the reasons for each investment and the conditions that would cause the thesis to change. Months 7–9: Expand selectively and support portfolio companies Continue sourcing while avoiding pressure to invest simply to meet a target. Compare new opportunities with existing portfolio exposure, especially by customer segment, regulatory dependency, revenue model and key-person risk. Make additional investments where they improve diversification or strengthen conviction in an existing theme. Establish quarterly reporting from each portfolio company covering revenue, cash position, customer retention, product milestones, regulatory developments and financing needs. Use the portfolio network to support hiring, enterprise introductions and regulatory expertise where useful. Months 10–12: Review, rebalance and plan the next year Assess each investment against its original thesis, using actual operating evidence rather than headline valuation or fundraising activity. Review concentration by theme, stage, geography, founder profile and regulatory exposure. Decide where to reserve follow-on capital, where to maintain exposure and where not to invest further. Review the sourcing funnel, diligence cycle time, conversion from first meeting to investment and the quality of post-investment reporting. Set the next year’s budget, portfolio construction priorities and updated screening criteria. Operating principles Evidence before expansion: company-reported metrics should be treated as claims until independently checked. Concentration with discipline: build around a small number of themes rather than investing across every fintech category. Regulatory awareness: regulatory alignment can create defensibility, but regulatory dependency can also extend sales cycles and increase execution risk. Reserve capital: keep capacity for follow-ons when operating evidence improves. No forced pace: a missed investment is preferable to an investment made without sufficient evidence. Immediate next step Set the annual budget, target number of positions and follow-on reserve; those three decisions will determine how large the initial pipeline and cheque sizes should be.
